Rashi on Shabbat 65a:10:1.english: Rabbi [is] that which we stated - That he is not concerned lest she remove [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:10:2.hebrew: פוטר בכובלת - ואוקימנא דהאי פוטר — מותר לכתחילה הוא, ואמר טעמא: מאן דרכה למיפק בכובלת? אשה שריחה רע, ולא שלפא ומחויא גנותה:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:10:2.english: Exempts with a bundle of fragrant herbs - And we established that this "exempts" means [it is] permitted ab initio, and [the Gemara] stated the reason: Whose manner is it to go out with a bundle of fragrant herbs? A woman whose odor is foul, and she will not remove [it] and show her shame.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:11:1.english: Beneath the net - Such as a woolen cap.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:11:2.hebrew: יוצאה בה - דלא חיישינן דילמא שלפא ומחוויא, דמיגלי שערה ומגניא בה, שהשבכה נוי הוא לשער:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:11:2.english: She may go out with it - For we do not suspect lest she remove [it] and show [it], as her hair would be uncovered and she would look unsightly thereby, for the hairnet is an adornment for the hair.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:10.hebrew: ובלבד שלא תפרוף לכתחלה בשבת - ובגמ' פריך: והאמרת רישא פורפת:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:10.english: As long as she does not fasten [it] ab initio on Shabbat - And in the Gemara it objects: But didn't you say in the first clause [that she] may fasten [it]?

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:2.english: Tzinit - It is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:3.hebrew: הבנות קטנות - שמנקבות אזניהם, ואין עושין נזמים עד שיגדלו, ונותנין חוטין או קסמים באזניהם, שלא יסתמו אזניהם — לוי"ה:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:3.english: The young girls - For their ears are pierced, but they do not make earrings [for them] until they grow up, and they place strings or chips in their ears so that their ears will not seal — [in Old French:] loie [a cord].

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:4.hebrew: ואפילו - רבותא קאמר: דאע"ג דלאו תכשיט נוי הוא, אורחא בהכי, ולא משאוי הוא. ויש מפרשין: חוטין שקולעת בהן שערה, דאסרינן לגדולה בריש פרקין — התם משום דשכיחא בהו טבילה, אבל קטנות דלא שכיחא בהו טבילה — שרי. ולשון ראשון הגון מזה: חדא, דקטנות נמי צריכות טבילה לטומאת מגע משום טהרות, ואף נדות נמי שכיחות בהו, כדתניא (נדה דף לב.): מעשה שהיה והטבילוה קודם לאמה; ועוד, מדקתני אפי' בקיסמין, איכא למישמע דחוטין נמי אאזנים קיימי, דאי חוטי הראש — לא שייך למיתני אפי' בקסמין:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:4.english: And even - [The Mishnah] states a novelty: that even though it is not an ornamental adornment, this is the ordinary practice, and it is not [considered] a burden. And some explain [the Mishnah's mention of] strings [as referring to strings] with which she braids her hair, which we prohibited for an adult woman at the beginning of our chapter; there, [it was prohibited] because immersion is common for them, but for young girls, for whom immersion is not common, it is permitted. And the first explanation is more fitting than this [one]: First, because young girls also require immersion for ritual impurity [contracted through] touch for the sake of [eating] ritually pure foods, and even menstruation is also found among them, as it was taught [in a baraita] (Niddah 32a): “An incident occurred where they immersed her before her mother.” And furthermore, since it teaches: “even with chips,” it can be inferred that the strings also refer to the ears; for if [it meant] strings for the head, it would not be relevant to teach “even with chips.”

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:5.english: Arabian [women] - Jewish women who are in Arabia.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:6.hebrew: יוצאות רעולות - דרך ערביות להיות מעוטפות ראשן ופניהם, חוץ מן העינים, וקרי לה בלשון ערבי רעולות. היינו הרעלות, דכתיב גבי תכשיטי נשים בספר ישעיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:6.english: May go out veiled - It is the practice of Arab women to have their head and their face wrapped, except for the eyes; and [the Mishnah] calls it in the Arabic language re'ulot. This is [the same as] “the veils” [ha-re'alot], which is written concerning women's adornments in the Book of Isaiah.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:8.hebrew: פרופות - שמעטפות בטלית, ותולה הרצועה בשפתה האחת כנגד צוארה, ובשפתה השנית כורכת אבן או אגוז, וקושרת הרצועה בכרך, ואין הטלית נופל מעליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:8.english: Fastened - That they wrap themselves in a cloak, and [a woman] hangs the strap on one edge opposite her neck, and in its second edge wraps a stone or a nut, and ties the strap around the bundle, and the cloak does not fall off her.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:9.hebrew: פורפת - כמו קרסים, דמתרגמינן: ״פורפין״. כל המחבר בגד לחבירו, קרי פריפה:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:12:9.english: She fastens - Like kerassim [clasps], which we translate [in the Targum as] purpin. Anyone who joins [one] garment to another, [it] is called perifah [fastening].

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:13:1.hebrew: בת ארעא - מכה שהיא תחת פרסת הרגל, וקושר בה סלע לרפואה:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:13:1.english: Daughter of the ground - A sore that is under the sole of the foot, and one ties a sela [coin] to it for healing.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:1.english: That is hard - For it is hard and protects the wound from thorns and pegs in the road.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:2.hebrew: שוכתא - ליחלוחית היוצא מן הכסף, ובלע"ז רוי"ל, ויפה למכה. שוכתא — כמו "דשתך טפי" דאלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כו.), ו"משתכין כנחשת" דתענית (דף ח.):
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:2.english: Rust - Moisture that exudes from silver, and in Old French roille [rust], and it is beneficial for a wound. [The word] "shukhta" is like "it corroded greatly" in [the chapter] Elu Metziot (Bava Metzia 26b), and "they become tarnished like copper" in Ta'anit (8a).

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:3.hebrew: ליעבד טסא - דכספא, טיבעא למה לי? אלא משום צורתא — דטיבעא מעליא למכה, ולאו שוכתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:3.english: Let him make a plate - Of silver; [if so,] why do I need a coin? Rather, [it is] because of the image — that the coin's [image] is beneficial for the wound, and not the rust.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:4.hebrew: ליעבד פולסא - עגול של עץ, ויצור עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:4.english: Let him make a pulsa - A round [piece] of wood, and let him carve [an image] upon it:

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:5.hebrew: אמר אביי ש"מ - ממתני' דנקט סלע:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:5.english: Abaye said: Learn from it - [He deduced this] from our Mishnah, which specified a sela:

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:6.hebrew: כולהו בהדדי מעלו לה - ולהכי נקט סלע, דאיתנהו לכולהו: אקושא, ושוכתא, וצורתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:14:6.english: All of them together are beneficial for it - And therefore [the Mishnah] specified a sela, as all of them are present [in it]: hardness, rust, and an image.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:15:1.english: Did not allow his daughters, etc. - [The Gemara] explains below the reason for all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:15:2.english: To lie next to each other - To sleep next to one another while they were still virgins.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:15:3.hebrew: מקואות ביומי ניסן - של מים מכונסין, או סמוך לנהר וממשיך לתוכן מי הנהר, וטובלות שם:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:15:3.english: Ritual baths in the days of Nisan - [He made ritual baths] of gathered water, or adjacent to the river, channeling the river water into them, and they would immerse there.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:15:4.hebrew: ומפצי ביומי תשרי - שטובלות בפרת, ומפני הטיט — שלא יהא חציצה — נותנות המפץ תחת רגליהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:15:4.english: And mats in the days of Tishrei - For they would immerse in the Euphrates, and on account of the mud — so that it should not be an interposition — they would place the mat under their feet.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:16:1.english: [That they] were colorful - And he was concerned about [their] removing [them] and showing [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:17:1.english: Who rub - They rub against one another out of sexual desire.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:1:1.english: He may spread them out in the sun - [This refers to] one whose garments were soaked on the road in rainwater.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:1:2.hebrew: אבל לא כנגד העם - שלא יאמרו: כבסן בשבת. האי תנא סבר, דמידי דמשום מראית העין מותר בחדרים:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:1:2.english: But not before the people - So that they do not say, “He laundered them on Shabbat.” This Tanna holds that anything [prohibited] due to the appearance of impropriety is permitted in [private] chambers.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:5:1.hebrew: עשתה לו בית יד - למוך שבאותו מקום, מהו למיסריה? דילמא שקלה וממטא לה בידים, דלא מאיס לאוחזה בבית יד שלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:5:1.english: [If] she made a handle for it - [Namely, for] the cloth in that place: What is [the ruling regarding] prohibiting it, [out of concern that] perhaps she will take it and carry it in [her] hands, since it is not repulsive to hold it by its handle?

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:5:2.hebrew: עשתה לה בית יד מותר - דלא אמרינן לא מאיס, אלא אפילו בבית יד מאיס:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:5:2.english: [If] she made herself a handgrip, [it is] permitted - For we do not say [that] it is not repulsive; rather, even with a handgrip, it is repulsive.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:6:1.hebrew: רבי יוחנן נפיק ביה לבי מדרשא - במוך שבאזנו, שהיה זקן והיתה לו צואת האוזן מרובה:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:6:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan went out with it to the study hall - With the wad of wool in his ear, for he was elderly and had an abundance of earwax.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:6:2.hebrew: וחלוקין עליו חבריו - מפני שלא היה קשור באזנו, והוא יוצא בו לרה"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:6:2.english: And his colleagues are in disagreement with him - Because it was not tied to his ear, and he went out with it into the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:6:3.hebrew: והא תני רמי והוא שקשור כו' - וכי קשור מיהא, אפילו לרה"ר מותר, ואמאי קאמר לבי מדרשו ולא קאמר לרשות הרבים? ומשני: דר' יוחנן קשור, ולא מיהדק הקשר. ולשון ראשון מיושב מזה:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:6:3.english: Didn’t Rami teach: And that is where it is tied, etc. - And if it is tied, in any event it is permitted even to the public domain; so why does [the Gemara] say “to his study hall” and not say “to the public domain”? And [the Gemara] answers that Rabbi Yoḥanan’s [cloth] was tied, but the knot was not tight. And the first version is better settled than this [one].

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:6:4.hebrew: הא דמיהדק - דר' יוחנן היה תוחב באזנו יפה ומהדק, ולא בעי קשירה; ודרמי בר יחזקאל — בדלא מיהדק. ל"א מתלמידי רבינו הלוי: דרבי יוחנן קשור הוה, ובית מדרשו סמוך לביתו הוה, ולא היתה רה"ר מפסקת:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:6:4.english: This [is a case] where it fits tightly - That of Rabbi Yoḥanan: he would insert [it] well into his ear and fit it tightly, so it did not require tying; and that of Rami bar Yeḥezkel is where it does not fit tightly. Another explanation, from the disciples of Rabbeinu HaLevi: Rabbi Yoḥanan's [wad] was tied, and his study hall was adjacent to his house, and no public domain intervened [between them].

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:7:1.english: For durshinei - For an ailment of the teeth.

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:8:1.hebrew: לא שנו - דחכמים אוסרין אלא של זהב, שמשונה במראה משאר שינים, ודילמא מבזו לה, ושקלה לה בידה וממטיא:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:8:1.english: They only taught - That the Rabbis prohibit only [in the case of a tooth] of gold, as it differs in appearance from the rest of the teeth, and perhaps they will ridicule her, and she will take it in her hand and carry [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 65a:8:2.hebrew: אבל של כסף - שדומה לשאר השינים, דברי הכל מותר — לשון רבותי. ולי נראה: טעמא דשל זהב משום דחשיבא ואתי' לאחויי, לכך אסור; אבל של כסף לא חשיבא ולא אתי' לאחוויי. וללשון רבותי קשיא לי: הא דאמר אביי, "רבי ור"ש בן אלעזר כו'", ואי טעמא דרבנן משום דחייכי עלה הוא, מאי שנא רבי דקחשיב ליה? רבנן נמי לאו לאחוויי חיישי! ויש לתרץ: דרבנן מיסר קאסרי מכל מקום, ורבי מתיר דקסבר לא חייכו עלה ולא שלפא להו. ומיהו, ה"ל למיחש: דלמא שלפא לה משום אחוויי? אלא לא שלפא, משום דאי מחוי לה גנותא היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 65a:8:2.english: However, [with regard to] a silver [tooth] - Because it resembles the rest of the teeth, everyone agrees [that it is] permitted — [this is] the phrasing of my teachers. But to me it seems: The reason for [a tooth] of gold is that it is valuable and she will come to show [it off, and] therefore it is prohibited; but [one] of silver is not valuable, and she will not come to show [it off]. And according to the phrasing of my teachers, that which Abaye said is difficult for me: "Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, etc." For if the Rabbis' reason is that they laugh at her, why is Rabbi distinct, that [Abaye] counted him? The Rabbis, too, are not concerned about showing [it off]! And one can answer: The Rabbis prohibit in any event, and Rabbi permits because he maintains that they do not laugh at her and she does not remove it. And yet, [Rabbi] should have been concerned lest she remove it in order to show [it off]? Rather, she does not remove it, because if she shows it, it is a disgrace [for her].

Tosafot on Shabbat 65a:14:1.hebrew: ליעבד לה פולסא - פ"ה: חתיכה של עץ, ויצור עליה צורה. ולפירושו ניחא מה שמקשים, דבעלמא אמר: "מאי אסימון? פולסא", ופ"ה התם: היינו דבר שאין עליו צורה; וקשה, דהכא משמע דפולסא הוא דבר שיש עליו צורה! ולפירש"י ניחא, דפירש: ליעבד פולסא בלא צורה, ויצור עליו הצורה. אבל לפיר"ת קשה, דפירש: אסימון הוי של מתכת ויש עליו צורה, אבל אינה חשובה ואינה יוצאה — אם כן, הכא מאי איריא סלע, אפילו אסימון? ושמא י"ל, דצורת סלע צריך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 65a:14:1.english: "Let him make a pulsa for her" - The Kuntres explained: A piece of wood, and let him carve an image upon it. And according to his explanation, what [people] question is resolved, for elsewhere [the Gemara] says: "What is an asimon? A pulsa," and the Kuntres explained there: That is an object that does not have an image upon it. And [this is] difficult, for here it implies that a pulsa is an object that has an image upon it! But according to Rashi's explanation [this] is resolved, as he explained: Let him make a pulsa without an image, and carve the image upon it. However, according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, [it is] difficult, for he explained [that] an asimon is of metal and has an image upon it, but it is not significant and does not circulate [as currency]. If so, here, why specifically a sela? Even an asimon [should suffice]! And perhaps one can say that the image of a sela is required.

Tosafot on Shabbat 65a:15:1.hebrew: ומפצי ביומי תשרי - פ"ה: מפני הטיט, שלא יהיה חציצה, ונותנות המפץ תחת רגליהן. ורבינו תם פירש שהיו נותנות מפצי זקופות, שלא יראו אותן העולם ויתביישו מהם ולא יטבלו היטב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 65a:15:1.english: "And mats in the days of Tishrei" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: Because of the mud, so that it should not be an interposition, and they would place the mat under their feet. And Rabbeinu Tam explained that they would set up upright mats so that people would not see them, and they would [otherwise] be embarrassed before them and not immerse properly.
